thread:
Maya: paging alert — SLO breach on streaming endpoints in us-west-2, p95/p99 escalating. Paging @Arun :rotating_light:

sre-bot: Incident created (P1) — 5123456790 — Latency SLO breach for /v1/stream Generate. Affected region: us-west-2. Automations: trace collection started.

Arun: on it, joining console now. seeing p95 ~ 600ms -> 1.2s and p99 jumping to ~7s from <2s. Streaming stalls (clients observe long tail stall, tokens not streaming).

Luis: looking at kv-cache metrics — eviction rate spiked 4x over last 8m, free slabs down to 12%. Prefill put pressure on small-entry slab pools. Decode queue is building up (decode-worker latency 90th -> 1.4s).

Maya: customer impact — CS flagged two customers seeing repeated streaming stalls, one reported intermittent 503s. Posting to status page now, tagging customers on the outage.

Jenna: CS update queued. Any quick mitigation other than restart?

Arun: quick mitigations we can do without full deploy: 1) throttle prefill concurrency for long-context sessions, 2) increase prefill eviction grace to reduce churn, 3) temporarily route heavy streaming traffic to smaller model variant (fall back routing).

Luis: agree. fragmentation appears to be caused by prefill-heavy sessions that allocate many small KV entries, then get evicted when decode backlog spikes. Prefill vs decode imbalance. We have fragmentation + slab starvation leading to slow allocations and stalls.

Maya: can you run a config push to increase small-entry slab pool and throttle prefill? paste commands here.

Arun: applying change now — running:```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/configs/cache -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"prefill_concurrency": 8, "small_slab_max_pct": 0.35, "prefill_eviction_grace_s": 60}'```
Executing. Will monitor eviction rate.

sre-bot: Config change queued by arun at 5123459800.

Arun: change applied. eviction_rate down ~38% in 90s, slab free up to 22%. p95 improved to ~420ms. p99 still shows tail events at ~4.5s.

Luis: good improvement. For p99 tail, I want to try two things: trigger a rolling restart of a subset of cache-workers to defragment slabs, and enable a temporary prefill backpressure on sessions > 8k tokens. Restart command (staggered):```
for node in cache-worker-1 cache-worker-2 cache-worker-3; do kubectl rollout restart deploy $node --namespace=cache -n us-west-2; sleep 45; done
```

Maya: agree, do rolling restarts one AZ at a time. Also open to enabling routing fallback to 7b model for streaming routes for 10m burst to buy time. Jenna coordinate CS message for the fallback.

Jenna: notifying customers about temporary fallback to smaller model for heavy streams in us-west-2. Status updated with mitigation steps.

Arun: kicking off rolling restart on canary pool now. Observing decode backlog drop after first node restart. p99 trending down to ~2.1s. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Deploy logs: cache-worker-1 restart completed at 5123459908. cache-worker-2 restart started.

Luis: I'm going to run our slab analyzer to check fragmentation index; if fragmentation > 0.6 I'll run slab-compaction job. Command: ``/opt/tools/kv-slab-analyzer --region us-west-2 --threshold 0.6``

Arun: traced a few sample requests — heavy prefix prefill patterns from a single customer job were dominating allocations. CS reached out to the customer and paused their long-batched runs. That removed a lot of pressure.

Maya: excellent. Customer paused job confirmed. That plus config change + rolling restart brought p95 back under SLO and p99 mostly stable. Remaining tail blips we should monitor for 2h.

Luis: taking over monitoring at handoff. I'll leave a note for followups: (1) permanent prefill throttling for long-context sessions, (2) slab pool tuning to be increased for small entries, (3) implement KV compaction as scheduled background job, (4) add alert for prefill/decode queue imbalance.

Arun: noted. Leaving traces and dashboard links: https://observability.internal/dash/streaming-latency?range=30m

Maya: handoff to Luis at 5123460050 — thanks team. Oncall rotation: @Luis you're the lead, @Arun stay available for escalation. Jenna, CS follow-up with customers and postmortem notes.

Luis: taking it — will update here if we see regressions. Adding runbook entry for slab starvation mitigation. :clipboard:

sre-bot: Incident resolved (degraded) at 5123460200 — SLOs restored to within targets. Postmortem scheduled in #postmortems tomorrow 09:30 PT.

Maya: quick recap / action items: 1) runbook updates (prefill knobs) assigned to Luis, 2) follow-up config PR to persist safe defaults (Arun), 3) customer comms (Jenna), 4) long-term work: KV compaction + prefill shaping (eng-runtime).

Arun: will open PR for config defaults and link to this thread.

Jenna: will send customer follow-ups and copy postmortem when ready.

Luis: will turn runbook into a checklist and add automated alert for eviction spike + decode backlog correlation.

Maya: thanks all, good job triaging quickly.
